_verify: Model IDs are best-guess placeholders. Confirm against each provider's current catalog and replace. Provider GROUP names (ollama-cloud / google / opencode-go / opencode-zen) are the stable routing keys; the models arrays are examples to edit.
goal: Route coding-agent work across LLM providers to save tokens and avoid single-provider usage limits (e.g. Ollama Cloud session 429). One provider GROUP per provider; task classes route to a preferred group with an ordered fallback chain.

ollama-cloud._modelsNote: glm-5.2:cloud is the current session model (confirmed). Add other Ollama Cloud catalog IDs as needed.
ollama-cloud.rateLimits: Session usage cap; returns 429 on exhaustion (observed). Fastest to exhaust under heavy subagent fan-out.

google._modelsNote: Best-guess; confirm current Gemini model IDs and replace.
google.rateLimits: Provider-dependent; generally higher quotas than Ollama Cloud session cap.

opencode-go._modelsNote: Populate with your OpenCode Go model IDs.

opencode-zen._modelsNote: Populate with your OpenCode Zen model IDs.

switchTriggers.rateLimited: Provider returned 429 / usage-limit / quota error -> skip to the group's fallbackAfter (or the routing entry's next fallback). Do NOT retry the same provider immediately.
switchTriggers.capabilityMismatch: Task needs long context (>200k tokens) -> google. Task needs strongest reasoning (verify/adversarial review, architect) -> opencode-zen or google. Task is bulk mechanical/explore -> ollama-cloud.
switchTriggers.costBudget: Prefer ollama-cloud for high-volume cheap work (explore, mechanical, general coding). Reserve google + opencode-zen for reasoning-heavy or long-context tasks. If a token budget is stated, estimate task cost before dispatch and pick the cheapest group that meets the capability bar.
switchTriggers.failure: Provider error / timeout / malformed response -> fall to fallbackAfter and record the failure.
switchTriggers.contextLength: If the task input + expected output may exceed a group's contextWindow, switch to a group whose window fits (google = 1M).

decisionProcedure: 1. Classify the task into one of: explore | mechanical | code-implementation | review | verify | plan | architect.
3. Before dispatch, evaluate switchTriggers against current conditions (recent 429? capability need? cost budget? context length?).
4. If a trigger fires, override preferred with the first viable group in the fallback chain.
5. Dispatch to the chosen group. On mid-task failure (429/error/timeout), fall to fallbackAfter and resume/redo from the last checkpoint.
6. Record which provider ran with the result (attribution) so token spend is traceable per provider.
